today.h: The Last Good News Failed: S&P -3.70% in a Seventh Straight Loss, Nasdaq -5.28% and Negative for the Year
today.d: Anthropic's record IPO did not revive the AI trade; it marked the top. The S&P closed in correction, 11.62% below its record, while the Dow sits 9.76% below its own; the Nasdaq gave back all of 2026, and the money went to Treasuries and staples while gold and bitcoin were sold for cash.
today.c1: The seventh straight loss was the worst of them. The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39, down 265.44 points, and closed 11.62% below its 10/6 record - a correction for the first time since March 2025. The Nasdaq lost 5.28% to 22,617.73 and is now 2.69% lower for the year. The Dow dropped 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33, a second session below 50,000. Ten of 11 sectors fell; staples were the only one up, +0.67%, while technology lost 7.27%. The trigger was the failure of the market's own good news: Anthropic, the biggest IPO on record, fell 8.50% on its second session, and Reuters reported the SEC is examining Nvidia's accounting. Nvidia fell 14.01% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index 10.73%. The VIX closed at 35.89, up 26.20%, its highest since April 2025. Treasuries and staples took the money; gold and bitcoin did not - December gold settled 4.64% lower at $3,514.50 and bitcoin fell 4.99% to $58,893, the difference between rotating and raising cash.
today.c4:
• The event: the biggest IPO ever closed its debut at $97.17 on 11/19 and at $88.91 on 11/20, -8.50%, after trading at $83.05 - the entire pop gone.
  • The trigger: Reuters reported the SEC is exploring Nvidia's accounting; NVDA -14.01% to $125.53 and a seventh straight losing week, the longest since 2008.
  • The transmission: the PHLX Semiconductor Index -10.73%, AMD -13.25%, Micron -13.90%, Broadcom -12.19%; all 20 semiconductor names in the Nasdaq-100 are in bear markets.
  • The hiding place: staples +0.67% was the only green sector, with Walmart, Costco, J&J and P&G all up about 1%.
  • The tell: gold -4.64% and bitcoin -4.99% fell alongside equities while the 10Y fell 12bp to 4.92% - cash was raised, not hedged.
  • The week: S&P -8.6%, Dow -8%, Nasdaq -10%, the worst week since April 2025.

chains.t: ① The AI Trade's Good News Became Its Exit
steps: Anthropic priced at $83 and closed its debut at $97.17 on 11/19; on 11/20 it closed at $88.91, 8.50% lower, after trading at $83.05
Nvidia fell 14.01% to $125.53 as a regulatory problem replaced the valuation debate
The semis followed: the PHLX Semiconductor Index -10.73%, AMD -13.25%, Micron -13.90%, Broadcom -12.19%
The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39, a seventh straight decline, and the Nasdaq 5.28% to 22,617.73, now negative for 2026
The bid went to Treasuries and staples, the only two places that held
Gold and bitcoin were sold rather than bought, so the exit was into cash rather than into havens
chains.d: The AI trade needed one more piece of good news to hold; it got the biggest IPO ever and still fell, and that is what turned an 8.2% pullback into an 11.62% correction.

chains.t: ② Nvidia: From a Valuation Problem to a Disclosure Problem
steps: The SEC is exploring possible accounting issues at Nvidia, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter
California's attorney general served Nvidia an investigative subpoena over whether advanced chips may have gone to China
NVDA closed at $125.53, down 14.01% and 33% lower in November
It is the seventh consecutive losing week, the longest streak since the 2008 financial crisis
Seventy-one of the Nasdaq-100's 101 stocks are in bear markets, including all 20 semiconductor and memory names, and the VIX ended at 35.89, the highest since April 2025
chains.d: A valuation debate can be argued with; a subpoena cannot, which is why Nvidia fell nearly four times as much as the S&P and carried the whole AI complex with it.

mtd.c1: November is a grind, not a crash. The S&P 500 is 8.83% below its 10/30 base of 7,580.07 and 11.62% below the 10/6 record of 7,818.93. The Nasdaq is 11.08% lower and the Dow 7.00%. The damage is concentrated where the year's gains were: technology is 16.99% lower and energy 13.58% lower, the two worst sectors, while staples (+1.16%) and communications (+0.13%) are the only two still above the line. The month's biggest single session was -4.36% on 11/5; the seven declines from 11/12 to 11/20 did more, taking 9.30% off the index.
